sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2020. Grammatical reconstruction: The Sogeram languages of New Guinea. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Latest comprehensive treatment of the Sogeram family; may update the status/classification of Magɨyi relative to Mum, though it is not expected to contain Magɨyi phonology.

sources.citation: OLAC: Open Language Archives Community combined catalog, 'OLAC resources in and about the Magɨyi language' [gmg], as of 2022-01-23 (Internet Archive copy; live host unreachable 2026-09-20).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: catalog lists exactly two resources for gmg - 'Glottolog 4.5 Resources for Magiyi' (language descriptions) and 'Magiyi: a language of Papua New Guinea' (Ethnologue 2018); no archive deposit (PARADISEC, Kaipuleohone, SIL-PNG, TLA) is registered for the code. Recorded here as evidence of absence, not as a descriptive source.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing on Magɨyi language structure; p. 32 only notes 'Akrukay people have regular contact with Magɨyi people of Vguvɨndɨ'.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2016. Magɨ: An undocumented language of Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 55(1): 199-224. doi:10.1353/ol.2016.0004 (ANU open repository copy hdl 1885/108658).
sources.note: Describes Magɨ [gkd] = Glottolog magi1243 (East Sogeram, sister of Aisi [mmq]) -- a DIFFERENT language from Magɨyi [gmg]; contains no mention of Magɨyi. Not usable for magi1244.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2015. A reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, lexicon, and morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara.
sources.note: Only mention of Magɨyi is p. 659 fn. 21: 'there may still be unsurveyed Sogeram languages to the west of Katiati; Joseph Brooks (p.c.) collected a brief wordlist on a lect from this area that his consultant referred to as "Magɨyi," which closely resembles Mum.' Nothing on Magɨyi phonology or stress (its phonology sections concern other Sogeram languages).

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2015. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 18th edition. Dallas: SIL International. Online entry 'Magiyi' [gmg] (the Internet Archive capture of 2015-06-27); also Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2019, 22nd edition, same entry (capture 2019-06-03).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: the open 18th/22nd-edition entries carry only Location (Vguvindi village), Language Status 6a/6a* (Vigorous), Classification, 'Language Resources: OLAC', and Writing 'Unwritten [Qaax]'; no Dialects, Typology, or Language Development fields; nothing on stress, accent or tone. Later editions (23rd, 2021 onward) are paywalled ('Unlock this profile with an Essentials plan').

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2013. Change Request Number 2013-029: create [gmg] Magɨyi (submitted by Joseph Brooks, UCSB). Dallas: SIL International. 8 pp. incl. comparative wordlist Magɨyi vs. Z'graggen (1980) Southern Adelbert languages.
sources.note: Nothing. Documents Brooks' 2012 encounter with one speaker, a short recorded text and short wordlist; wordlist (pp. 6-8) is segmental only, no stress marks; closest cognates with Paynamar/Manat and Mum.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2013. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: [gmg] Magɨyi (requester Joseph Brooks), associated with CR 2013-029. 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. States written literature/recordings: 'None'; closest language Mum [kqa]; classification TNG > Madang > Southern Adelbert Range > Josephstaal; location Vguvɨndɨ village.
